metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive extraction from Colonial Office List 1910. Extracted data from 93 colony and administrative files including geographical entities, prosopographical data (people and positions), institutions, economic statistics, infrastructure, demographics, and historical events. Data preserves exact historical spelling and terminology from source documents. All salaries, coordinates, and numerical data extracted exactly as written in source.

places.name: Trinidad
places.description: Island lying about 16 miles to the eastward of Venezuela. Average length about 48 miles, average breadth 35 miles. Separated from the continent of America by the Gulf of Paria. Amalgamated with Tobago by Order in Council on 1st Jan 1890.

places.name: Port of Spain
places.description: Chief town and principal port, situated on a gently inclined plain near the north-east angle of the Gulf of Paria. Port of registry. Ten miles of electric tramway and 500 miles of telephone constructed.

places.name: San Fernando
places.description: Town and port about 30 miles south from Port of Spain. Has an elective municipal council and mayor.

places.name: Tobago
places.description: Island formerly in the Windward Islands, amalgamated with Trinidad by Order in Council on 1st Jan 1890. By Order in Council of 20th Oct 1898, became a ward of the Colony of Trinidad and Tobago from 1st January 1899.

places.name: Transvaal
places.description: South African territory. Annexed by Great Britain in 1877, First Boer War 1880-81, Second Boer War 1899-1902. Peace signed May 31, 1902. Full responsible government conferred December 6, 1906.

places.name: Johannesburg
places.description: Major city in the Transvaal, center of gold mining industry

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.modern_name: Cape Province (now part of South Africa)
places.description: Colony in southern Africa with Legislative Council of 26 elected members and House of Assembly of 107 elected members. Includes territories of Bechuanaland and Pondoland.

places.name: Dominion of Canada
places.description: Confederation formed July 1, 1867 by Imperial Act 30-31 Vict. c. 3. Original provinces: Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia. Subsequently added Manitoba (1870), British Columbia (1871), Prince Edward Island (1873), Alberta and Saskatchewan (1905).

places.name: Malta
places.description: Mediterranean island colony. Chief port and seat of government.

places.name: Pitch Lake
places.description: Pitch lake situated in the ward of La Brea, distant by water about 30 miles from Port of Spain. Of considerable value. Leased to English Concessionaires for 21 years from 1st January 1888, extended for further 21 years from February 1909.

institutions.name: Executive Council of Trinidad and Tobago
Legislative Council of Trinidad and Tobago

composition.description: Reconstituted in 1898. Consists of the Governor, Colonial Secretary, Attorney-General, Solicitor-General, Auditor-General, Inspector-General of Constabulary, Director of Public Works, Surgeon-General, Protector of Immigrants, Receiver-General, Collector of Customs, and such other persons (unofficial members) as Governor may appoint. Unofficial members hold seats for five years and are eleven in number.

institutions.function: Legislative body for Trinidad and Tobago

institutions.name: Legislative Council

composition.description: Contains 15 members, nominated by Governor for five years. Appointments to fill vacancies made by Governor in Council. President appointed by Governor in Council.

institutions.function: Upper chamber of Transvaal Legislature established under Letters Patent of December 6, 1906

institutions.name: Legislative Assembly

composition.description: Contains 69 members returned by single-member constituencies, of whom 34 represent the Witwatersrand area

institutions.function: Lower chamber of Transvaal Legislature established under Letters Patent of December 6, 1906

composition.description: Consists of Chief Justice and six Puisne Judges

institutions.name: Senate
institutions.function: Upper chamber of Parliament of Canada

institutions.name: House of Commons
institutions.function: Lower chamber of Parliament of Canada

institutions.name: Trinidad Dock and Engineering Company, Ltd.

composition.description: Formed and registered in 1906 to carry into effect an agreement for provision of floating graving dock and workshops. Company to remain British in character.

institutions.function: Operates floating graving dock and workshops in harbor off Chaguaramas. Over-all length 365 feet, clear beam 56 feet (expandable to 65 feet). Lifting power 4,000 tons. Government pays subsidy to supplement net earnings.

institutions.name: Malta University
institutions.function: University providing education in theology, law, medicine, and arts

economic_data.notes: Does not include annual appropriation for interest and sinking fund

infrastructure.name: Port of Spain to Arima Railway
Couva Line
infrastructure.notes: 24 miles in total from Port of Spain. Opened in 1880

infrastructure.name: Internal Telegraph System
infrastructure.notes: Constructed by Government. Direct telegraphic communication with British Guiana, Grenada and Saint Croix, and thence via Canada or United States with Europe

infrastructure.name: Wireless Telegraph System
infrastructure.notes: Established in 1906 between Trinidad and Tobago. 318 messages from Trinidad to Tobago and 309 from Tobago to Trinidad in 1907-8. Recently established with British Guiana but not open for general use pending further experiments

infrastructure.name: Central South African Railways
infrastructure.notes: Includes lines of late Netherlands South African Railway, late Orange Free State Government Railways, and Pretoria-Pietersburg Railway. Length as of 31st August 1909. Further 65 miles from Belfast to Lydenburg nearing completion

infrastructure.name: Electric Tramway
infrastructure.notes: Electric tramway in Port of Spain and environs

infrastructure.name: Telephone System
infrastructure.notes: Telephone system in Port of Spain and environs, extends to some country districts
